documents.generated_document: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Follow-up diabetes and hypertension. HPI: 68 y.o. male established patient presents for routine follow-up of his T2DM and HTN. He reports his home fasting blood sugars have been running higher lately, mostly in the 180-220 range. He admits to some dietary indiscretions over the holidays but has been trying to get back on track. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or lower extremity edema. He does note some mild intermittent blurry vision over the last month. No polyuria or polydipsia. HTN has been well controlled at home with systolic readings in the 120s. ROS: General: No weight loss or fatigue. Eyes: Positive for intermittent blurry vision. CV: Negative for orthopnea or claudication. Neuro: Negative for numbness or tingling in feet. PMH: T2DM, Essential hypertension, Hyperlipidemia. MEDICATIONS: Metformin 1000 mg BID, Lisinopril 20 mg daily, Atorvastatin 40 mg daily. ALLERGIES: NKDA. VITALS: BP 134/82, HR 76, Temp 98.6 F, Wt 212 lbs, BMI 30.4. PHYSICAL EXAM: General: Well-appearing, no acute distress. HEENT: PERRLA, EOMI. CV: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Extremities: Warm and well perfused, no peripheral edema. Monofilament testing intact bilaterally. ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with hyperglycemia: Currently uncontrolled. Recent A1c from last week resulted at 8.9%, up from 7.6% six months ago. We discussed dietary modifications at length. Given the elevated A1c and home readings, I will add Glipizide 5 mg daily before breakfast. Ordered CMP and repeat A1c in 3 months. Placed referral for annual diabetic retinopathy screening given the blurry vision. 2. Essential Hypertension: Stable on Lisinopril. Will continue current dose. 3. Hyperlipidemia: Stable on Atorvastatin. Patient to follow up in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.
documents.Justification: The E&M code 99214 is supported by a moderate level of Medical Decision Making for an established patient. The number and complexity of problems addressed is moderate, involving one chronic illness with exacerbation/poor control (Type 2 Diabetes with hyperglycemia) and two stable chronic illnesses (Hypertension and Hyperlipidemia). The risk of complications and/or morbidity is moderate due to prescription drug management (initiating Glipizide for the uncontrolled diabetes). Two out of three MDM elements meet the moderate threshold, qualifying the encounter for 99214.
